chunks: He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid reported to me from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Awramah, from Ismail ibn Aban al-Warraq, from al-Rabi ibn Badr, from Abu Hatim, from Anas ibn Malik, who reported that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, said:

"O Anas, perform ablution frequently, and God will increase your lifespan. And if you are able to remain in a state of purity throughout the night and day, then do so, for if you die in a state of purity you will die a martyr.
And pray the noon prayer, for it is the prayer of those who return to God in repentance. And perform many voluntary prayers, so that the guardian angels will love you.

And greet with peace whomever you meet, and God will increase your good deeds. And greet with peace your household, and God will increase your blessings. And venerate the elders among the Muslims, and be merciful to their young, and I shall come with you on the Day of Resurrection like these two" -- and he brought together the middle finger and the index finger.

key_terms.الأوابين: Al-Awwabin -- those who frequently return to God in repentance
key_terms.الحفظة: Al-Hafazah -- the guardian angels who record deeds
key_terms.الطهور: Tahur -- ritual ablution/purification, the act of maintaining wudu
key_terms.شهيدا: Shahid -- martyr; here indicates the elevated spiritual status of one who dies in purity
key_terms.صلاة الزوال: Salat al-Zawal -- the noon prayer at the sun's zenith
key_terms.طهارة: Taharah -- the state of ritual purity

ai.seo_question: What advice did Prophet Muhammad give to Anas ibn Malik about purity and worship?
ai.summary: In this hadith narrated from Anas ibn Malik, a companion who served the Prophet personally for ten years, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) provides him with a comprehensive set of practical instructions covering ritual purity, prayer, social greetings, and respect for others. The advice concludes with the Prophet's promise that following these practices will bring the follower close to him on the Day of Judgment, illustrated by the iconic gesture of holding two fingers together.
